indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B1.5.1.1: Recognise the importance of personal hygiene
indicator.objective: Explain the need for bathing and know how it is done

skills.description: Describe the correct steps for bathing

misconceptions: Bathing is just playing with water.
You only need to bathe when you are visibly dirty.
Using water alone is enough; soap is not needed.
You should share your sponge and towel with friends.

questions.stem: Why do we bathe?
hints: Think about what happens when you sweat.
questions.explanation: We bathe to remove dirt and sweat from our bodies.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think bathing is just for fun.

questions.stem: Which of these is used for bathing?
questions.explanation: Soap is used with water to clean the body.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think any liquid is soap.

questions.stem: What do you use to dry your body after bathing?
hints: It is soft and absorbs water.
You hang it in the bathroom.
questions.explanation: A towel is used to dry the body after bathing.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think any cloth is a towel.

questions.stem: How often should you bathe?
questions.explanation: You should bathe every day to stay clean and healthy.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think bathing once a week is enough.

questions.stem: What is the first step in bathing?
questions.explanation: The first step in bathing is to wet your body with water.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think you apply soap to a dry body.

questions.stem: What happens if you do not bathe regularly?
options: You smell bad and can get sick
questions.explanation: If you do not bathe regularly, you will smell bad and germs can make you sick.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think skipping baths has no consequences.

questions.stem: Kofi is going to bathe. Which of these should he take with him?
questions.explanation: Kofi needs soap, a sponge, and a towel to bathe.

questions.stem: Why is it important to use soap when bathing?
options: Soap helps remove dirt and germs
hints: Water alone does not kill germs.
questions.explanation: Soap helps to remove dirt and germs from the skin.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think water alone is enough.

questions.stem: After applying soap and scrubbing your body, what should you do next?
hints: You need to wash the soap off.
questions.explanation: After scrubbing with soap, you must rinse your body with clean water.
questions.misconception: Pupils may dry off without rinsing.

questions.stem: Which of these should you NOT share with a friend?
questions.explanation: You should not share your sponge because it can spread germs.
questions.misconception: Pupils may share personal items without knowing the risks.

questions.stem: Ama played football and is sweating. What should she do?
hints: She needs to clean her body.
questions.explanation: Ama should bathe with soap and water to clean off the sweat and dirt.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think sweating is fine without cleaning.

questions.stem: Name two items used for bathing.
questions.explanation: Soap, sponge, water, and towel are used for bathing.

questions.stem: Why should you bathe before going to school?
options: To look clean and stay healthy
hints: You don't want to smell bad.
questions.explanation: You should bathe before school to look clean and stay healthy.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not see the link between hygiene and health.

questions.stem: What is the correct order for bathing?
options: Wet body, apply soap, scrub, rinse, dry
Dry body, apply soap, wet body, scrub
Apply soap, dry body, wet body, scrub
Scrub, wet body, dry body, apply soap
questions.explanation: The correct order is wet body, apply soap, scrub, rinse, and dry.
questions.misconception: Pupils may do steps out of order.

questions.stem: Which of these items is NOT used for bathing?
questions.explanation: A book is not used for bathing.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think any object in the bathroom is for bathing.

questions.stem: Kofi says 'I only bathe when I see dirt on my skin.' Why is this wrong?
options: Because dirt and germs can be on the skin without you seeing them
questions.explanation: You should bathe regularly because dirt and germs can be on your skin even if you cannot see them.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think visible dirt is the only reason to bathe.

questions.stem: Demonstrate to your teacher how to bathe a doll correctly.
hints: Don't forget to dry the doll.
questions.explanation: This tests the practical steps of bathing.

questions.stem: Draw some of the items you use for bathing.

criteria.description: Draws at least two correct items (e.g., soap, sponge, towel)

hints: What do you use in the bathroom?
questions.explanation: This tests identification of bathing items.

questions.stem: Write down two reasons why bathing is important.
hints: Think about how you feel after playing.
questions.explanation: Bathing removes dirt and prevents sickness.

questions.stem: Explain the steps you take to bathe.
hints: What do you do after scrubbing?
questions.explanation: The steps are wet, soap, scrub, rinse, and dry.
